name: Hanamel
title: Jeremiah's Cousin and the Land Sale
summary: Hanamel was the son of Shallum and cousin of the prophet Jeremiah. He is known for selling a field in Anathoth to Jeremiah, a purchase that served as a prophetic sign that property would once again be bought and sold in Judah after the exile. This event took place while Jerusalem was under siege by the Babylonians.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's Word About the Land Purchase
keyEvents.description: God revealed to Jeremiah that his cousin Hanamel would come and offer him the chance to buy his field in Anathoth, in accordance with the right of redemption.

keyEvents.title: Hanamel Visits Jeremiah in the Guard Court
keyEvents.description: As the Lord had said, Hanamel came to Jeremiah in the guard court at the king's palace and asked him to buy the field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: The Purchase of the Field
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah bought the field from Hanamel for seventeen shekels of silver, wrote a deed, sealed it, and had witnesses confirm it, as a sign of hope for the future.

keyEvents.title: The Deeds Given to Baruch
keyEvents.description: In the presence of Hanamel and the witnesses, Jeremiah gave both the sealed and the open deeds to Baruch son of Neriah, instructing him to place them in an earthenware jar for safekeeping.

keyEvents.title: Prophetic Meaning of the Purchase
keyEvents.description: The purchase from Hanamel became a prophetic sign: the Lord promised that houses, fields, and vineyards would once again be bought in the land, despite the impending destruction and exile.
